figures.title: From information to an approved order
figures.caption: Workflow schematic used to explain both studies. The language model interprets bounded inputs; numerical tools calculate orders and independent checks control execution. This is not an additional experimental result.

figures.title: Three kinds of information
figures.caption: Evidence classification. These categories must be distinguished even when they appear together in a planning record. Natural lost demand is not observed.

figures.title: The computational panels
figures.caption: Both panels have thirty store–product series. M5 has three selected food products across ten stores; RetailNet has twenty-six products and twenty-nine stores. Full-release validation is separate from panel performance evaluation.

figures.title: Sales were often availability-constrained
figures.caption: Complete pinned release: training and evaluation files. Hourly and daily percentages use different denominators. Operating hours are 06:00–21:00. These observations identify availability conditions; they do not quantify true lost demand.

figures.title: How the experiments answer different questions
figures.caption: Study map. M5 and RetailNet include numerical and matched-reader work. Separate forecasting and fresh-product calculator analyses use RetailNet and contain no language-model calls.

figures.title: Verified repair under an inventory-field fault
figures.caption: Improved M5 pilot; thirty series, fourteen days, two shared seeds. Simulated cost uses the M5 study monetary conventions. The matched rule-based reader achieved the same results.

figures.title: Reader comparisons lie on the equality line
figures.caption: Improved pilot: sixteen matched scenario/seed/recovery comparisons. Some points overlap because outcomes are equal. Exact daily actions also matched; equal cost and service are not evidence of incremental LLM superiority.

figures.title: Unadjusted-sales LightGBM led the main forecast test
figures.caption: Official evaluation, 114 fully stocked panel-days out of 210. Lower WAPE is better. Models were selected before evaluation unsealing. These are numerical methods, not LLM forecasts.

figures.title: Approval policy had to fit the new setting
figures.caption: Matched cap transition at the original two seeds, 13 and 29, for the LLM-with-repair configuration; the reader counterpart is equal. Original cap 1,500, training-selected cap 1,850. Follow-up is exploratory and reuses the holdout.

figures.title: Verified repair under an inventory-field fault
figures.caption: Exploratory calibrated follow-up; thirty series, seven days, thirty seeds. Reused holdout. Cost is an index, not retailer currency. The matched rule-based reader achieved the same results.

figures.title: The repair benefit varied across seeds
figures.caption: Exploratory follow-up, inventory-field fault, thirty paired seeds. Cost decreased in 26/30 seeds; orange points show the four adverse cost outcomes. Fill increased in 30/30. Simulation seeds are not independent stores or historical weeks.

figures.title: Lower cost came with lower service
figures.caption: Normal scenario, the same thirty seeds and seven-day horizon. Conventional optimizer: primary numerical study. Approval workflow: exploratory calibrated follow-up. Both had zero actual committed-rule violations. No overall-winner claim is supported.

figures.title: Fresh-product service and expiry must be read together
figures.caption: Separate age-aware calculator analysis, thirty seeds per cell, assumed demand multiplier 1.25. Waste denominator is opening stock plus receipts. Shelf lives are hypothetical. No LLM calls; units and supply differ from the main optimizer study.

figures.title: A valid stockout flag should inform the decision
figures.caption: Sixty separate calculator runs, thirty shared seeds, three-day life and assumed demand multiplier 1.25. Hold-on-stockout is a deliberately defective ablation, not a strong competitor. Neither configuration uses an LLM.

figures.title: Within-setting repair effects
figures.caption: Descriptive comparison, inventory-field-fault scenario. M5: improved pilot. RetailNet original: fixed-cap primary study. RetailNet calibrated: exploratory reused-holdout follow-up. Economic scales and horizons differ; the reader achieves the same effects as the LLM.

figures.title: Tools contained inappropriate recovery requests
figures.caption: Request-level observations, shown separately by study. All stale-source repair requests were refused. Cached reader imports are not additional model judgements. Correct formatting does not establish correct tool choice.

figures.title: A proposed route to operational testing
figures.caption: Managerial recommendation derived from the findings. This operational pilot was not conducted as part of the dissertation and does not represent an observed deployment result.

figures.title: Numerical controls: service and active-rule compliance
figures.caption: Original numerical study; thirty seeds per policy/scenario and seven days. Cost follows M5 model conventions. Violated checks are not reference-only action deviations and can exceed the number of affected days. These are conventional policies, not the matched LLM-versus-reader experiment.

figures.title: Historical forecasting context
figures.caption: Retained reduced-panel pre-main-study backtests; thirty bottom series and 112 aggregate nodes. The two origins overlap and are descriptive. Lower is better. This is not a full M5 competition ranking or an LLM forecasting result.

figures.title: Artificial-mask hourly reconstruction
figures.caption: Training-validation test on originally fully stocked days; 6,930 hidden target hours and 2-, 4-, 8-hour masks. Lower MAE is better. This does not identify naturally unserved demand and contains no LLM calls.

figures.title: Numerical controls: service and active-rule compliance
figures.caption: Primary numerical study; thirty seeds per policy/scenario and seven days. Costs are indices. The approval policy retains the original cap. Violated checks are not reference-only action deviations and can exceed the number of affected days. These are conventional policies, not the matched LLM-versus-reader experiment.

figures.title: Cost depends on demand and shelf-life assumptions
figures.caption: Separate age-aware calculator with raw history and thirty seeds per cell. Neither assumed demand nor shelf life is observed natural ground truth. No LLM calls; this cost index is not pooled with the main optimizer.
